newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Palm says 3.2 or 3.3 pct deficit acceptable.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Palm says 3.2 or 3.3 pct deficit acceptable.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm said on Tuesday Germany could still qualify for European monetary union even if the country failed to exactly meet the three percent deficit target.
"If it is 3.2 percent or 3.3 percent, that will not rule Germany out automatically," Palm said in a speech.

Palm also criticised Bonn for attempting to push through a revalution plan of Bundesbank gold reserves that would have impacted its 1997 budget deficit in a bid to ease its path into the new single European currency at its start in January 1999.
Palm said Bonn had damaged Germany's negotiating position in the European Union by suggesting the measure and had reduced the German public's faith in the EMU project.
He also said the project may not have been approved by European authorities.
